reason: E4 directly supports transforming lamellar eutectic into ultrafine duplex microstructures with improved strength-ductility synergy and a microcrack-arresting mechanism, but it uses only rolling/annealing, not additive manufacturing. E2 shows LPBF can refine interphase spacing and enhance strength in the same alloy system, but does not demonstrate the vermicular morphology or combined processing route. E1 and E3 provide general evidence that processing alters microstructures and properties in HEAs, but do not address eutectic lamellar-to-vermicular transformation or the specific combined route.
premises: Eutectic high-entropy alloys can be processed to transform straight lamellar into ultrafine duplex microstructures
Such microstructural transformation increases heterogeneous phase boundaries
Increased heterogeneous phase boundaries pin dislocations and arrest microcracks
This dual mechanism synergistically improves strength, ductility, modulus, and fracture resistance
Combined cold rolling, annealing, and additive manufacturing can achieve this vermicular microstructure
